patterns: Almost all announced data center gas supply goes through existing interstate or intrastate transmission, or through a short new line from a transmission or local distribution company. Only the Intensity-Rainbow line in North Dakota explicitly ties directly into processing plants, and it is a long 36-inch transmission-class pipe. The clearest wellhead or gathering-type cases (Chevron near Pecos, New Era Helium near Odessa) involve producers burning their own gas on site with little or no new pipe described. Most projects publish no length or diameter, so row counts would depend on later regulatory filings. Several large Permian projects have not named a pipeline operator.
not_found: No source I could open showed a gathering system or processing plant residue line built or planned for a data center in Oklahoma, Pennsylvania wellhead supply, Targa, Enterprise, Atlas, or Basin Electric. Range, CNX, Expand Energy, Hut 8, and Diversified (fuel cells, Virginia/West Virginia/Kentucky) turned up nothing about dedicated lines. Poolside's gas path and Shippingport's delivery path were not confirmed. Many publisher pages (S&P, Energy Transfer, globenewswire, DCD) returned 403 so were not cited. Crypto: none found. Kinetik and Targa earnings calls named no data center customers.
